events.continuity_hook: This opens Erin's next planning episode after the fixed-date Virginia Beach family trip is wrapped up.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Madison versus Milwaukee routing, Sunday arrival timing, hotel area, car versus rideshare, and the schedule details to confirm before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After the Virginia Beach weekend, Erin is assigned to a late-July certification workshop in Madison tied to a new analyzer software rollout. The workshop has an optional Sunday evening check-in, a Monday morning lab start, and a Wednesday afternoon finish that may run late if the final practical module backs up. Denver-to-Madison choices are mostly one-stop, with a Chicago routing that has one tight return connection, a Minneapolis routing with steadier layover time, and a Milwaukee option that saves some airfare but adds a long drive. Hotel choices include a campus-area block with easy walking but limited recovery amenities, a Middleton suite hotel with strong guest scores, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness access, and a downtown property with paid parking. The return day, rental-car need, and exact workshop end time are still unresolved.

events.continuity_hook: This refines the Madison certification plan after the workshop schedule becomes firmer.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the outbound flight, return-day choice, Middleton hotel hold, compact rental decision, room notes, and seat requests before the better fares move.
events.scenario_brief: The organizer confirms that the Madison workshop starts Monday at 8:00 a.m. and the final practical module should end Wednesday around 3:30 p.m., with no required Thursday attendance. A Sunday afternoon Denver-to-Madison flight through Minneapolis has the cleanest arrival setup, while the Wednesday evening return through Chicago now shows a short layover that would be uncomfortable if the module runs late. A Thursday midday return keeps the connection simpler and adds only one hotel night. The Middleton suite hotel can hold a quiet king room with a fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room; the campus block is still walkable but has poorer amenities and a higher nightly parking charge. Erin needs to settle whether the calmer Thursday return is worth the extra night and whether to book a compact rental for the campus commute.

events.continuity_hook: This is the Madison pre-trip adjustment after Erin chose the extra hotel night and Thursday return.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to move to the earlier outbound, clean up seats, set rental pickup timing, plan campus parking, and run the final certification packing checklist.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before Madison, Erin has the Sunday-to-Thursday plan booked, with the Middleton suite hotel and a compact rental in place. The airline moves the Denver departure later and compresses the Minneapolis connection to about 40 minutes; a no-cost switch to a slightly earlier Denver departure would restore a more comfortable transfer. The hotel reconfirms the quiet-room note, fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room. The workshop site sends parking instructions that require a visitor permit each day, and the return aircraft swap removes her window-seat assignment. Weather around the connection city looks unsettled for Sunday, so the main open decision is whether to accept the earlier outbound and rebuild the seat selections now.

events.continuity_hook: This starts a mixed work-and-leisure episode after the Madison certification trip is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked plan for Erin’s Phoenix flights, spouse flight timing, work hotel, Sedona stay, rental strategy, and the schedule questions that affect the extension.
events.scenario_brief: After Madison, Erin’s August calendar adds a Phoenix metro training week with a possible Sedona weekend add-on with her spouse. A Monday afternoon setup at a Tempe reference lab is penciled in, Tuesday and Wednesday clinic sessions may split between Scottsdale and Mesa, and Thursday wrap-up could be in Glendale or handled remotely. Denver-to-Phoenix nonstop options are easy, but her spouse would need a separate Thursday or Friday arrival if they keep the Sedona extension. Work hotel candidates include a Tempe suite property with a strong guest score, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness access; a Scottsdale hotel closer to one clinic but with resort fees; and an airport hotel that only helps with late arrivals. Sedona hotels trade balcony-view rooms, recovery amenities, cancellation rules, and summer pricing. The work-end time, spouse arrival date, rental-car size, and whether to commit to Sedona are open.

events.continuity_hook: This narrows the Phoenix and Sedona plan once the work sequence and spouse availability become clearer.
events.interaction_goal: Book Erin’s outbound, spouse’s inbound, the shared return, Tempe lodging, Sedona lodging, rental class, seat requests, and room notes before the cancellable Sedona rate disappears.
events.scenario_brief: The Arizona coordinator confirms a Monday 2:00 p.m. Tempe setup, Tuesday Scottsdale training, Wednesday Mesa session, and Thursday Glendale wrap-up expected to end by 4:00 p.m., with no Friday debrief. Erin can take a Sunday afternoon nonstop from Denver to Phoenix, and her spouse can join on a Thursday evening nonstop if they keep the same rental vehicle through the weekend. A Friday morning spouse arrival is cheaper but would cut into the Sedona day. The Tempe suite hotel can hold a quiet king room through Friday checkout with free parking, pool, hot tub, fitness room, and an in-room fridge. A Sedona hotel can hold a king room with balcony request, pool, hot tub, and fitness access for Friday through Monday, but the cancellable rate expires soon. The remaining decisions are spouse arrival timing, midsize versus standard SUV, and whether to lock the Sedona hotel now.

events.continuity_hook: This closes the Arizona work-and-Sedona extension plan after the bookings are in place and late operational details start shifting.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final logistics pass for flight timing, seats, rental pickup, hotel trade-offs, spouse arrival, heat and smoke backup plans, Sedona room choice, and Monday return timing.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before Arizona departure, Erin has the Sunday Denver-to-Phoenix nonstop, Tempe hotel through Friday checkout, spouse’s Thursday evening inbound, Sedona weekend hotel, midsize SUV, and Monday return booked. The spouse’s inbound is moved about 50 minutes later, which still works but makes Thursday dinner unrealistic. The return aircraft swap separates their seats, with only one window seat still open nearby. The Tempe hotel reports the hot tub will be closed during Erin’s stay, though the pool and fitness room remain available; switching hotels would add a worse commute and higher parking. The Sedona property says the balcony is still request-only and offers a guaranteed first-floor patio room for an added charge. A heat advisory and possible smoke haze may affect hiking plans, and the rental agency is showing limited SUV inventory.
